A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSD study. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and their methods, equations, figures, and tables can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments on WikiMIA, ArXivTection, BookMIA, and BookTection, including ablations and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original Pile evaluations, domain-transfer tests, and hyperparameter analyses in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: FSD still fine-tunes on auxiliary non-members using next-token prediction, subtracts fine-tuned scores from pretrained scores, and thresholds the difference. Equations (4)–(5) and threshold selection are unchanged; the new experiments do not redefine the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation across 20 Pile subsets, extending coverage to domains such as code, email, legal text, forums, and subtitles while retaining the original four benchmarks. It also evaluates mixed-domain auxiliary data and an unrelated-domain fine-tuning scenario.

E2.justification: Perplexity, Lowercase, Zlib, and Min-k% remain the evaluated detection baselines. The new Pile and robustness experiments reuse this comparator set, and the existing LoRA/AdaLoRA/IA3 comparison is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces a Pile protocol using Pythia-6.9B training/validation membership, 30% validation-data fine-tuning, and disjoint balanced evaluation. New studies specify a 2,800-example BookC2 test set, mixed-domain sampling, and learning-rate/rank/epoch grids. The reported All-ablation test counts also change from 536/549 to 599/558 members/non-members between v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 10; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds BookC2 data-size sensitivity curves (Figure 6), mixed-domain and unrelated-domain auxiliary-data tests (Table 16), and learning-rate, LoRA-rank, and epoch sensitivity analyses (Table 17). These substantially expand robustness evidence beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: v1 Appendices B.1–B.2 specify data-split seed 42; the corresponding v2 passages omit it. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals. This is reduced seed disclosure, not evidence of changed seeds or run counts.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, but substantial new results appear. v2 Tables 2 and 15 report Pile mean Perplexity AUC of 0.503 for the baseline and 0.625 with FSD. Table 16's unrelated-domain test reports Perplexity AUC of 0.68/0.52 and Zlib AUC of 0.57/0.64 for baseline/FSD, exposing both deterioration and improvement. Figure 6 and Table 17 add data-size and hyperparameter results.

T1.justification: The formal detection setup, model-access assumptions, scoring definitions, loss, and FSD equations remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: auxiliary unseen data enables FSD to improve existing detection scores, and using such data is the claimed novelty. Pile extends the supporting evidence without redefining these contributions; the broad universal-improvement wording remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning domain mismatch, relative rank/epoch insensitivity, and learning-rate dependence. Its Limitations paragraph replaces v1's explicit warning that success may reflect member/non-member distribution differences with concern about auxiliary-data quality. The unrelated-domain failure interpretation is broader than Table 16 supports, since Zlib improves there.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-repository access information in the abstract and documents sampling procedures and parameter ranges for the new experiments. Existing hardware, software, learning rate, batch size, and default epoch disclosures remain essentially unchanged. Repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive novelty positioning are unchanged. v1 Section 6 is retained as v2 Appendix A; the Pile experiments reference Maini et al., which was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, revises method headings, moves Related Work to Appendix A, and adds Ethical Statement and Acknowledgement passages. Most existing prose and the main explanatory sequence remain intact, so this is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial new displays: the Pile summary and detailed comparisons, domain-transfer and hyperparameter tables (Tables 2 and 15–17), and the two-panel BookC2 curves in Figure 6. Existing figures and tables are retained with relocation, resizing, and limited caption changes.

improvement.justification: The Pile experiments use explicit training/held-out membership, providing an important additional validity check beyond v1's timestamp-based benchmark analyses. Domain-transfer and sensitivity tests substantially strengthen evidence about where FSD works and fails. These validation gains outweigh the removed seed disclosure and dropped distribution-confounding caveat in Limitations, although the unchanged universal claims remain broader than the reported results support.
